title.narrative: North Macedonia Public Finance and Competitiveness DPL

description.narrative: The Public Finance and Competitiveness Development Policy Loan (DPL) supports North Macedonia's efforts to strengthen the sustainability of public finances, improve market competition, and reduce the regulatory burden on businesses. After a period of political stalemate, the government in office since May 2017 embarked on an ambitious reform program to safeguard macroeconomic stability, improve citizens well-being, strengthen competitiveness, and pursue the country's aspirations for European and international integration. The government's Economic Reform Program (ERP) 2019-21 aims to strengthen revenues, improve public financial management, increase market competition, make the environment for doing business more attractive, and strengthen labor market and social protection. The DPL supports reforms that aim to safeguard fiscal sustainability, improve market competition, and lower the regulatory burden on businesses in the context of renewed impetus for European and global integration. This operation has been closely coordinated with international partners (including the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the European Commission (EC), United States Agency for International Development (USAID), and other bilateral partners) to ensure that policy support and technical assistance are complementary. The DPL objectives are aligned with the World Bank Group Country Partnership Framework (CPF) FY19-FY23.
The proposed DPL supports reforms to strengthen public finances, improve market competition, and reduce the regulatory burden in North Macedonia.

title.narrative: Increased social assistance coverage of the bottom quintile, female-led households

comment.narrative: <p>The RI has been met. The reform proved particularly timely as the country faced the COVID-19 crisis. Reform of the social service system is also progressing with more and more cases under case management.</p>

title.narrative: Increased social assistance coverage of the bottom quintile, total

comment.narrative: <p>The RI has been met. The reform proved particularly timely as the country faced the COVID-19 crisis. Reform of the social service system is also progressing with more and more cases under case management.</p>

<p>The RI has been met, but parts of the reform supported, namely introduction of a progressive tax rate and removal of exemptions on capital income taxation, have been postponed to 2023.</p>
<p> </p>

title.narrative: Average number of bidders per competitive procurement procedure increased.

comment.narrative: <p>The RI has been met but with a delay. After dropping to 3.34 in 2019, the average number of bidders per procedure increased to 3.63 in 2020. Improved transparency, fairer competition principles, and lower costs increased the number of appeals by the firms, up by 22% in 2019.</p>

<p>The RI has been met and reached 2.42 percent of GDP in 2019. Arrears owed to the private sector have been mostly cleared and have declined from more than 50 percent of total arrears to about 43 percent. Due to the impact of the COVID-19 crisis, in 2020 arrears went up, reaching 2.65 percent of GDP, but are still below the target value.</p>

<p>The PAYG pension deficit did narrow in 2019 reaching <em>4.53% of GDP </em>but less than expected because of a rush to retire ahead of the reform. However, introduction of ad hoc indexation at the end of 2019 based on the growth of minimum and average wages partially reversed the reform and had already wiped out some of the reform gains in 2020.???</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of electricity consumers able to choose an electricity supplier on the open market

comment.narrative: <p>The RI has been met. Since the deregulation, over 90% of businesses have switched electricity providers and decreased their electricity costs.</p>

title.narrative: Share of fossil fuel consumption subject to excise taxation increased.

comment.narrative: <p>The RI has been met. Progress has also been made in tobacco taxation by broadening the tax base.</p>

title.narrative: Risk-based inspection introduced in inspectorates relevant for businesses.

comment.narrative: <p>The RI has been met with a delay. Annual working plans for 2021 are finalized for 14 inspectorates, of which 4 launched risk-based inspections in January 2021 (State Labor Inspectorate, State Market Inspectorate, State Inspectorate for Environment, and State Agriculture Inspectorate).</p>
